life-is-a-dream: Pedro Calderón de la Barca's 1635 masterpiece is the crown of Spain's Golden Age theater. Prince Segismundo, raised in a tower believing himself a beast, is briefly made king — then told it was all a dream. The play asks whether life itself might be a dream, and whether we should act well regardless. Philosophical, poetic, and still performed worldwide.
de-amicitia-scipio-s-dream: Cicero's De Amicitia — on friendship — joined with Scipio's Dream, his soaring vision of the cosmos, in one classic volume. Rome's greatest prose at its most humane and lofty. Essential Latin for every student of the classics. Laelius speaks for friendship; Scipio dreams of the starry heavens.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-abbey-of-st-e: This piece treats St. Emmeram of Regensburg, the Bavarian house of ancient fame. Its library held treasures of the early Middle Ages. George Cyprian Alston gives its story. Old Germany's bookish pride. Its scriptorium saved many a classic from oblivion.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-abel-son-of-a: This 1913 reference piece on Abel, son of Adam — the first martyr, slain by Cain. John Tierney gathers scripture and tradition. His blood cried from the ground, says Genesis. A brief entry on a timeless figure. His lamb was the first acceptable offering.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-abraham: This 1913 reference article on Abraham — the patriarch, father of the faithful. James Howlett gathers Genesis, tradition, and archaeology. Ur of the Chaldees, the covenant, and Mount Moriah all find their place. The fullest Catholic account of the great patriarch. Three faiths still call him father.
